label: 1.3.0-opus-high
messages: /tokenwise:route implement a feature from a written spec, about 12 files
/tokenwise:route review a six-file diff in a repo I know well

result:
- Phase: implementing a feature from a written spec, about 12 files.
- Model and effort: Sonnet at `medium`. Open `/model`, pick sonnet, set effort to medium and press `s` to switch for this session only. On the bench, Sonnet at medium passed every run of this task class at 17% of the cost of Opus at xhigh. That was a small test project, and 12 files is larger than it, so the figure is a guide rather than a guarantee. The evidence comes from `claude-sonnet-5`. If you're on a newer Sonnet, the row was measured on the older one. Ultracode doesn't fit here because this is execution against a spec, not independent high-judgment slices.
- Boundary: if the spec came out of a planning session, make sure it's saved to a file, then `/clear` and switch. Changing model or effort without clearing re-processes your whole current context, and `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until the next `/clear`, so clearing right after reading it costs least.
- Delegate: send test runs, log reading and any lookups in the existing codebase to subagents so only summaries come back. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=haiku` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE=1` so they run on Haiku. Otherwise they inherit the session model. Start the implementation from the spec file, not from memory.
- Done when: the tests the spec calls for pass, the project's lint and typecheck are clean, and no existing test file was edited to make them pass.
- You give up: Sonnet has less headroom when the spec is ambiguous or when the 12 files interact in ways the spec doesn't spell out. Where Opus might resolve those on its own, Sonnet is more likely to need a retry.
- Escalate when: if Sonnet skips files, doesn't run the tests or stops partway, raise effort to `high` or `xhigh` and stay on Sonnet. On the bench, Sonnet at xhigh cost less per completed task than Opus at medium. If it ran the tests and still gets the logic wrong, move to Opus at `medium`, then `xhigh`. For one hard step, try `ultrathink` in that prompt first. Before any switch on a large context, write down where the work stands and `/clear`.

- Phase: review a six-file diff in a repo you know well
- Model and effort: Opus at `low`. Switch for this session only with `s` in the `/model` picker and the `/effort` slider. On the bench's six-file diff, Opus at low found all five planted defects in 3 turns. Opus at high found the same five in 13 turns and cost 3.3x as much. Those runs used `claude-opus-5`, which is what `opus` points to now.
- Boundary: run `/clear` first if the conversation already holds earlier work. If you change model or effort on a warm context instead, your whole current context gets re-processed; `/context` shows how big that is. This answer stays in your context until your next `/clear`, so routing just before one costs least.
- Delegate: nothing. Six files is small enough to review in the main context. If you need to run tests to confirm a finding, send that to a subagent so only the result comes back.
- Done when: every finding gives a file:line and an input that makes it fail. Check the list against the diff before you fix anything.
- You give up: low effort thinks less and makes fewer tool calls. It can miss a defect that only shows when you trace across files. Sonnet at high costs less but missed one of the five defects in two of three runs, so it isn't the cheaper fallback here.
- Escalate when: a defect turns up later that the review should have caught. If files were skipped or it didn't trace far enough, raise effort to `high`. If it read the right code and still misread it, switch model. For a single tricky file, put `ultrathink` in that prompt before changing either. Ultracode doesn't fit this: it cost 9.5x `xhigh` on this same review for the same five defects.
